provenance_rules.rule: Acceptance criteria carrying a bracketed identifier such as [TIA-AC-04] come from the PRD; those without one are additions the backlog introduced.
provenance_rules.applied_as: Every FLTIQ-62 AC bracketed [TIA-AC-NN] is classed origin=prd; every unbracketed AC is classed origin=backlog. The single AC bracketed [FLTIQ-60] does not match the [TIA-AC-NN] pattern this rule describes -- it is a backlog-added AC that cross-references its governing dependency ticket, not a PRD-origin marker. Classed origin=backlog with dependency=FLTIQ-60.

_sources_schema_notes: Each entry in sources[]: {type, id, found_on, relationship, authority, version?, retrieved_at, fields_used?}.
'found_on' is the issue key where this artifact was actually located (the story, the Epic, a specific sub-task key, or a linked-issue key) -- never assumed from its type.
'relationship' is the structural path that led there: primary | parent | subtask-of-story | subtask-of-epic | issue-link | prose-dependency | cache-copy.
Do not pre-fill this array with stub rows or guessed ids. An unresolved source belongs in missing_sources, not here with an empty id.

conflicts.outcome: Not a genuine conflict. PRD 1 and its epic-wide child stories (FLTIQ-52, FLTIQ-53) state these three criteria apply to 'each screen/flow in this document/epic' -- a scope that includes the landing page even though the page itself has no dedicated PRD section. The story's 'no PRD requirement' statement is accurate for page-specific content; it does not exempt the page from cross-cutting PRD requirements.

conflicts.domain: scope (whether pricing/commercial-terms content ships on this page)
conflicts.outcome: Resolved by requester decision, 2026-09-21 (spec.md Clarifications, Session 2026-09-21). The requester authorized the design's line to ship as designed, explicitly on record as interim/placeholder copy created without marketing input and subject to future revision -- not the committed commercial policy the story's pricing exclusion was written to prevent. This is the adjudication constitution I's precedence policy anticipates: a business-intent question neither source alone settles, now settled in writing by the party with authority to settle it.
